title: Round trips: money that comes back to someone connected with the organization or the decision
question: Where does City money leave for one organization and then reach a party connected with that organization or with the decision to fund it?
finding: 87 paths were found: 39 of the kind “grant onward to an organization that shares a leader”; 24 of the kind “officer or director paid as an outside contractor”; 14 of the kind “grants in both directions between two city-funded organizations”; 8 of the kind “rent paid to the organization’s own insider”; 2 of the kind “contractor’s staff gave to the supervisor who sponsored the nonprofit’s funding”. The largest is Low Income Investment Fund to Felton Institute, $7.9 million (2021-2025). Of 20 pairs of a nonprofit and a supervisor who sponsored its funding, 2 had a contractor whose staff gave to that supervisor within three years, $750 in all: on that test nothing of size was found.
how: Five kinds of path in four families, each taken from a record already on file. (1) A City-funded organization grants onward to another whose tax return lists the same name among its leaders (grant-chains screen). (2) An organization's own return reports rent or a lease with one of its insiders (buildings screen), or lists one of its officers among its highest-paid outside contractors (people screen). (3) Two City-funded organizations grant to each other. (4) A supervisor is named as sponsor of a budget add-back or Board file for a nonprofit, the nonprofit's return lists a contractor, and people who name that contractor as employer gave to the supervisor's committees (campaign transactions; employer name must equal the contractor's name). Amounts and years are as the records give them.
limits: Being linked is not being involved: nonprofits share board members, buildings and auditors all the time, and San Francisco is a small city. A group is a place to look, ranked by how many independent signs sit inside it. None of these paths shows that City money, rather than other income, made the onward payment. The returns here disclosed the insider leases and payments; whether they were fairly priced is not shown. A shared name on two returns is a name match, not a confirmed person; funders and grantees often share a board member on purpose. Staff of a contractor give to campaigns for their own reasons. Pays (grant, contract or rent): sub-grants and specialist contractors are how programmes are delivered. Shares an officer or director (name match): board members often serve several organizations, and affiliates share leaders as a matter of course. Gives to the campaign of: campaign donations are reported, with limits on amounts.
